text.p: Chiang Hsiao-yuan, grandson of the late Taiwanese Nationalist leader Chiang Kai-shek, has died at the age of 48 after suffering from cancer of the oesophagus, a Taipei hospital said on Monday.
Chiang Hsiao-yuan was the son of the late president Chiang Ching-kuo and his Russian wife Faina Vakhreva Chiang.
Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek has been regarded as a national hero since 1949 when he led the Nationalist government to Taiwan after it lost China's civil war to Communist troops. He died in 1975.
His family's status began to fade when his son Chiang Ching-kuo launched democratic reforms in the late 1980s.
Despite his family background, Chiang Hsiao-yuan never played an active role in Taiwanese politics. He worked for several Nationalist Party-owned businesses before moving to Canada in 1989.
But he had been a critic of Taiwan's current president, Lee Teng-hui.
